To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphorylation of Eschericia coli CheY protein, which transduces chemotactic signals from the flagellar motor to the motor protein, FliM, increases CheY binding affinity for FliM, and this is mediated by a novel allosteric pathway that involves a specialized conduit between the phosphorylation site and FliM binding site.
phosphorylation of CheY protein transduced by the flagellar switch protein FliM drives compaction of CheY protein and that this compaction is allosterically coupled to FliM binding.

the conformational changes of the CheY protein that are induced by binding to its target protein FliMN are coupled to the allosteric network of CheY and that these changes are responsible for the activation of CheY.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the flagellar motor response to chemoreceptor stimulation and the molecular basis of the cooperative response.
the mechanism of CheY allosterism, a paradigm of molecular recognition.
understanding the mechanism of CheY activation by its binding target at E. coli flagellar motor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CheY.FliM allosteric network is organized into four dynamically coordinated sectors, with the substitutions mapped to sectors that are around the D57 phosphorylated residue or the FliM binding interface.
the simulations and experiments provide an unprecedented view into the molecular mechanism by which CheY is allosterically primed for motor binding.
the simulations and experimental results together show that FliM increases the affinity of CheY for the flagellar motor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CheY.FliM allosteric network can be described in terms of a series of communities of residues.
CheY is a highly dynamic allosteric protein with a specialized conduit for FliMN priming.
CheY is a molecular switch with an allosterically coupled network that is primed by the flagellar FliM protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CheY conduction pathway is not binary but graded and that the substitutions are localized at the phosphoryl pocket and the FliMN binding site to modulate the conduction.
the CheY allosterism is more complex than previously thought and the network is not a simple binary switch.
the CheY allosterism is a complex, multilayered network with many features that have not been appreciated thus far.
